clue.text: Escorted former President at start of exile into 'republic

indicators.note: the president and the starting letter are put into the republic, which wraps around them

parts.note: Chad is an African republic
Juan Peron was a former president of Argentina

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word exile is taken

explanation.surface: A deposed head of state is escorted back into his country at the outset of exile.
explanation.walkthrough: Peron was the Argentine leader exiled in 1955; Chad is in central Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaperone someone is to escort or accompany them, so the past tense matches escorted.

clue.text: One's inflexible, attaching ship to part of foreshore

parts.note: a hard is a firm sloping stretch of shore used for landing boats
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A stubborn person ties a vessel up on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: A HARD is a firm landing place on the foreshore, a sense the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sticks rigidly to a policy and will not compromise is a person who is unbending.

clue.text: Accommodation suitable for toffs overlooking a university city

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces before stand above the A, looking down on it

parts.note: a pad is informal for a flat or lodging
U is the old label for upper-class usage, suitable for the posh

explanation.surface: A posh flat with a view of a university town.
explanation.walkthrough: U (upper class) is a convention from 1950s discussions of posh English usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Padua in northern Italy is home to one of Europe's oldest universities.

clue.text: Rescued male cried uncontrollably

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are jumbled out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A man was saved and wept without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reclaimed has been recovered or saved, so it is a synonym of rescued.

clue.text: Something to muffle a hooter at mealtime?

definitions.text: Something to muffle a hooter at mealtime?

parts.words: Something to muffle a hooter at mealtime?
parts.note: a hooter is slang for a nose, and the feeding bag a horse wears at mealtimes covers its nose

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests silencing a car horn or a siren; a hooter is slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's feeding bag hangs over its muzzle, so it does cover the snout at mealtimes.

clue.text: Foreign character in alluvial area

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet, the fourth one
a fan of silt deposited at a river mouth

explanation.surface: A stranger found living on river silt.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the Greek letter D, and the river-mouth deposit is named after its triangular shape.

clue.text: Check out patient

definitions.meaning: to ... a place is to inspect it, often before a robbery
a doctor speaks of a person under treatment as a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Case means to reconnoitre a place, and a doctor calls someone being treated a case.

clue.text: Plant that's excellent, remarkable and mostly delicate shooting up

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole run of pieces is read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
rare means unusual or remarkable

indicators.note: the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: nice can mean fine or delicate, as in a nice distinction

explanation.surface: A fine, unusual garden plant, delicate and growing fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts NICE to NIC; 'shooting up' reverses AIRARENIC to give the plant. AI stands for A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Cineraria is a daisy-like flowering plant often grown in pots.

clue.text: With love at heart, good person in charge of a classical school

indicators.note: the letter for love goes in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A kindly, good person runs an old-fashioned academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' puts O (love) in the middle of ST + IC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoics were a school of ancient Greek philosophy, and stoic as an adjective means belonging to them.

clue.text: Channels for leading manufactured goods

indicators.note: one piece comes in front of the other

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
ducts are tubes or channels carrying fluid

explanation.surface: Pipes for top-quality manufactured items.
explanation.definitionFit: Products are things made for sale, which is what manufactured goods are.

clue.text: Left working man in city

parts.note: on means operating or functioning
a don is a man, especially a university fellow or a Mafia boss

explanation.surface: A worker left for the city.
explanation.definitionFit: London is the capital city of England.

clue.text: Animal seen in a cold area on mountain

indicators.note: in an across clue the first pieces come after the mountain, placed on it

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A beast spotted in a chilly patch on a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American relative of the llama, kept for its wool.

clue.text: Buffet food provided by lady

parts.note: to buffet is to strike repeatedly, to beat
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: A woman supplies the meal for a buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' reads as a spread of food, but it is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrice is a woman's given name, so a lady fits as a definition by example.

clue.text: Sign of life in dank house

indicators.note: the letters run inside the two words dank and house

explanation.surface: A symbol of vitality turns up in a damp home.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh is the ancient Egyptian looped cross symbolising life.

clue.text: Own a dictionary maybe and get angry

definitions.meaning: to possess a book full of vocabulary, read literally
to quarrel or argue heatedly with someone

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, having a dictionary means possessing words; idiomatically the phrase means to argue crossly.

clue.text: Qualified person puts heart of case to judge — her?

definitions.text: Qualified person puts heart of case to judge — her?

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
the gist is the essential point of a matter
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A graduate puts the core of a case to a woman for her verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a magistrate weighs the gist of a case, and 'her?' hints at a female one.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a lay judge in a lower court who decides the core of each case.

clue.text: What can you do with a bed? Defer your decision

definitions.text: What can you do with a bed?
definitions.meaning: a bed is something to lie on and slumber on, read literally
to put off deciding until the next day

explanation.definitionFit: Literally you can slumber on a bed; idiomatically the phrase means to delay a decision overnight.

clue.text: Experience a duck? It's something that happens in sport

parts.note: to touch can mean to experience or feel
down is the soft feathers of a duck

explanation.surface: Feeling a duck is a common sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a duck' suggests a cricket score of nothing, but it supplies the bird's soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchdown is a scoring play in American football and the grounding of the ball in rugby.

clue.text: Care for port?

definitions.meaning: the protective care of God over the world
the capital of Rhode Island, a harbour city in the USA

explanation.surface: Looking after a fondness for fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine; it is the Rhode Island harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is divine care, and it is also the name of the port city in Rhode Island.

clue.text: Trap set up to get one girl or another

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned upwards

parts.note: a gin is a snare for animals
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A snare is laid to catch one woman or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses GIN to NIG; add ELLA (one girl) and the answer is a different girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella is itself a woman's given name, so it is a second girl beyond the first.

clue.text: Neighbour has an objection

parts.note: a but is a reservation or objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: The person next door raises a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to border on or adjoin, the verb sense of neighbour.

clue.text: Speaking in a, particular way, adding line into picture

indicators.note: the letter for line goes inside the picture word

parts.note: a drawing is a picture

explanation.surface: Talking in a special manner while sketching a line into a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray comma is the newspaper print; it does not affect the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawling means talking slowly with drawn-out vowels, a distinctive manner of speech.

clue.text: Steward to pass through the ring

definitions.meaning: a medieval manager of an estate or a local official
a sailing term for threading a rope through a ring or block

explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a steward or bailiff, and to reeve is to thread a rope through a ring.

clue.text: Plans to put out a side

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed, put out of order

explanation.surface: Schemes to field a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are plans or schemes, in the sense of having an idea to do something.

clue.text: Very comfortable additional feature Henry needed

parts.note: a plus is an extra advantage or feature
Hy is an old written abbreviation of the name Henry

explanation.surface: Henry wanted an extra feature to make things comfy.
explanation.walkthrough: Hy as a short form of Henry is in Chambers but is rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Plushy is an informal adjective for luxurious and cosy, like plush fabric.

clue.text: Show in America a celebrity short

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States

indicators.note: the final letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: a hero is a celebrated, admired person

explanation.surface: In the States a star is put on a brief show.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone is to lead or show them into a place.

clue.text: In love, fail to hold attention

indicators.note: the fail word holds the attention word inside it

parts.note: an engine or a battery that fails is said to die
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone smitten cannot keep anyone's interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearie, like love, is an affectionate form of address.

clue.text: Meal in Chunnel awful — nothing gets eaten

indicators.note: the round letter is swallowed by the jumbled word
the letters of the word are rearranged badly

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Food on the Channel Tunnel train is so bad that none is eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns CHUNNEL into LUNCHEN; 'gets eaten' puts O (nothing) inside it. The Chunnel is the Channel Tunnel between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Luncheon is a formal word for the midday meal.

clue.text: Where you're reputed to see monster's head

definitions.text: Where you're reputed to see monster
definitions.meaning: the Scottish loch said to hold a famous monster

explanation.definitionFit: Loch Ness is home to the legendary monster, and a ness is a headland.

clue.text: Slight knowledge of affair Carol concealed

indicators.note: the carol word hides the affair word within it

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a matter is an affair or business

explanation.surface: A slight knowledge of a love affair hidden by a woman called Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name; it is the verb meaning to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight superficial knowledge, as of a language.
